title: Hubaekje
capsule: Later Baekje (후백제, Hubaekje) was founded in 900 CE by Gyeon Hwon, a former Silla garrison general who claimed descent from the ancient Baekje kingdom and established his capital at Wansanju (modern Jeonju). At its height the kingdom controlled the southwest of the Korean peninsula and posed a serious challenge to both Later Silla and Later Goguryeo (Taebong). Gyeon Hwon briefly captured the Silla capital Gyeongju in 927, killing King Gyeongae, but after a crippling defeat at the Battle of Gochang (930) against Wang Geon's Goryeo forces, the state collapsed; Goryeo absorbed it in 936 and completed the unification of Korea.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Later Baekje's territorial extent is partially reconstructed from Goryeosa chronicles and is broadly agreed upon for the southwestern peninsula; precise boundaries of control versus nominal suzerainty are uncertain.
